hook: Reversing a knot's direction can change its complexity in Thompson's group, as the knot 8_17 shows.
summary: Thompson's groups can build every link, and the Thompson index counts how complex a knot is within them. The author proves bounds from the Jones and HOMFLY-PT polynomials and computes the indices for prime knots up to 13 crossings by exhaustive search with certified results. Hundreds of non-invertible knots differ from their reverses, and one index separates the Conway knot from its mutant. Some indices are only fully determined up to 8 to 12 crossings.
title: Thompson indices of knots and the invertibility problem
